in_hebrew.name: נבוכדנצר
in_hebrew.meaning: נבוכדנצר: מי שאמר נבו ה' יגן צדק
in_hebrew.long_meaning: נבוכדנצר הוא שם שמקורו במסופוטמיה ומורכב משני אלמנטים: 'נבו' - השם של האל הבבלי של החכמה והכתב, ו-'צדק' או 'נצר' שפירושו 'ה' יגן' או 'צדק של נבו'. השם נבוכדנצר מורכב מהאלמנטים האלה ומשמעותו 'נבו, ה' יגן צדק' או 'צדק של נבו'. המלך נבוכדנצר השני היה שליט בבל מפורסם ששלט בתקופת הגלות של עם ישראל.

in_greek.name: Νεβουχadnezzαρ
in_greek.meaning: Νεβουχadnezzαρ: όνομα σημαίνει ους Νεβουχadnezzαρ εστιν αρετή
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Νεβουχadnezzαρ είναι όνομα προερχόμενο από την Βαβυλώνα και συγκεκριμένα από το όνομα του βασιλιά Νεβουχadnezzαρ Β', ο οποίος ήταν γνωστός για την κατάκτηση της Ιερουσαλήμ και την εξορία των Ιουδαίων. Το όνομα αποτελείται από το 'Νεβου', που σημαίνει 'Νεβου, ο θεός της σοφίας', και το 'χadnezzαρ', που σημαίνει 'προστατεύω' ή 'δικαιοσύνη'. Η σημασία του ονόματος είναι 'Νεβου, προστατεύω τη δικαιοσύνη'.

in_latin.name: Nebuchadnezzar
in_latin.meaning: Nebuchadnezzar: nomen significat Deus Nebo iustitiam donabit
in_latin.long_meaning: Nebuchadnezzar est nomen derivatum ex Mesopotamia, compositum ex duobus elementis: 'Nebo', quod est nomen Dei Babylonici sapientiae et scripturae, et 'Nezar' vel 'Nezer', quod significat 'Dominus iustitiam donabit' vel 'iustitia Nebo'. Nomen Nebuchadnezzar significat 'Deus Nebo iustitiam donabit' vel 'iustitia Nebo'. Rex Nebuchadnezzar secundus fuit celeberrimus rex Babylonis, qui regnavit tempore exsilii populi Israel.

in_english.name: Nebuchadnezzar
in_english.meaning: Nebuchadnezzar means 'may Nebo protect the king' or 'Nebo, protect the boundary'
in_english.long_meaning: The name Nebuchadnezzar originates from the Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar II, who conquered Jerusalem and exiled the Jews. Etymologically, it comes from the Akkadian language, combining 'Nebo', the Babylonian god of wisdom and writing, and 'Nergal' or 'Nezar', meaning 'to protect' or 'boundary'. The name signifies 'Nebo, protect the king' or 'may Nebo protect the boundary'. Nebuchadnezzar is a significant figure in the Bible, particularly in the Book of Daniel, where he is portrayed as a powerful ruler who acknowledges the God of Israel.

biblical_reference.note: Nebuchadnezzar II is a prominent figure in the Book of Daniel, representing a powerful king who conquers Jerusalem and exiles the Jews, yet also experiences divine intervention and conversion.

data.cultural_impact: Nebuchadnezzar is a critical figure in Jewish and Christian history. He is remembered as the monarch who conquered Jerusalem and carried the Jews into captivity in Babylon. His name has become synonymous with the desolation and suffering inflicted upon the Israelites during this period. Nebuchadnezzar's rule also marked the beginning of the Babylonian Empire, which would later be succeeded by the Persian Empire under Cyrus the Great, who would ultimately facilitate the return of the Jews to their homeland.
data.spiritual_significance: The story of Nebuchadnezzar serves as a powerful illustration of the consequences of pride and the importance of recognizing God's sovereignty. In the biblical account, Nebuchadnezzar's hubris leads him to make an image of himself and order all his subjects to worship it. When three Hebrew emissaries refuse, they are thrown into a fiery furnace, but emerge unscathed, demonstrating God's power and protection. Nebuchadnezzar is then humiliated by being driven from human society and living like a wild beast until he acknowledges God as the true ruler. Through this experience, Nebuchadnezzar comes to understand that "the Most High is sovereign over all kingdoms on earth and sets up kings to rule them according to his will" (Daniel 4:17). This message of recognizing God's sovereignty continues to resonate with people today, reminding us to keep our pride in check and submit ourselves to the divine will.
